caption: GPS lost. Sensor jammed. 5 seconds to total failure.
text: This aircraft has lost GPS. Jamming is corrupting its only motion sensor, and in a few seconds that sensor dies completely. We still have to say exactly where it went.

caption: Textbook maths: 1,256 m off.  Driftlock: 0.77 m.
text: Do the textbook maths on this sensor and you end up more than a kilometre away. The real path never left a small room. Driftlock keeps it in the room, with under a metre of error.

caption: Track 3: one dying IMU in, one pose per row out
text: This is Samsung's Track Three challenge. One damaged sensor file goes in. One pose for every row comes out, inside eight megabytes of memory, and twenty milliseconds of compute for each second of flight.

caption: Real run · one command · one thread · offline
text: Here's a real run. One command, one thread, fully offline. In well under a second, Driftlock reports what the jamming did: a thousand dead rows, forty nine gaps, frozen readings, duplicates and spikes. And every input row gets exactly one pose back.

caption: A detector for every kind of damage
text: We read the organisers' own degradation script, and built a detector for every kind of damage it causes. We even caught a mismatch. The script expects accelerometer columns first, but the real files put the gyroscope first. Driftlock works out the order from the data itself.

caption: Repair · attitude both ways · drift locked on a true time grid
text: Then it repairs the stream, tracks orientation forwards and backwards through the whole flight, and locks down drift on a true time grid, so a two second dropout stays two seconds long.

caption: IMU dead: dead reckoning for the final 5 s
text: When the sensor dies, Driftlock keeps flying blind. It carries the last velocity and turn rate forward, and fades them out over the final five seconds.

caption: Scored with evo, exactly like the judges
text: We score ourselves the same way the judges do, with the open source evo tool. Our own evaluator matches it to within a millimetre.

caption: 30 degraded runs · 3 drone flights never tuned on
text: Across thirty degraded runs, including three drone flights we never tuned on, Driftlock never blew up, while textbook maths lost kilometres. And we say it plainly: on drones, a motion sensor alone barely beats standing still. On handheld motion, we cut the error by over twenty percent.

caption: 5.97 MB heap · ~3 ms per second of flight
text: All of it runs in under six megabytes, at about three milliseconds per second of data. That's six times inside the time budget, small enough for a headset or a drone.

caption: Driftlock · github.com/hannielvinu/PathFinder
text: Driftlock. A dying sensor in, a trustworthy path out. The code, the mission report, and every result are on GitHub.
